- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/runs (route, bridged from symbol getRun — its route source's handler names it), /automation/:name/runs/:runId (route, the route ledger binds it to client method automation.getRun))_

> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0f967d22d50ced459f455516495a246b94697a21` — the merge of head `8ec36611b9ba9005b191cb11e3378a636a57a53e` into base `c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0f967d22d50ced459f455516495a246b94697a21 && git checkout 0f967d22d50ced459f455516495a246b94697a21
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900 8ec36611b9ba9005b191cb11e3378a636a57a53e && git checkout -B drift-repro c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900 && git merge --no-ff 8ec36611b9ba9005b191cb11e3378a636a57a53e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c48cd2c103a9dfa99313a67a3ec622291d793900` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `84b980b361bab0e34fccba340894617e21ae07cb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts + content/docs/references/automation/builtin-node-config.mdx, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/map-node.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/map-cancelled-item-resume.test.ts, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, .changeset/27971-map-cancelled-item.md; read for the collision and refusal claims: packages/spec/src/automation/flow-bound-variable-name.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-history.ts

Reviewed 2026-10-30T15:38Z · PR #28176 · card #27971 · ruling 6523833308 (letter A) · base `origin/main` a3d24c99 (merge-base 2695de71) · the whole diff read as the net diff against `main` at the head; nothing checked out, built or run.

Check-runs on the head at this reading — completed: Auto Label, Dogfood Regression Gate (its three matrix shards skipped), Plan Test Core shards, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check PR Size, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Flag docs affected by code changes, PR-body guards, filter, Spec property liveness — all `success`; skipped by their own predicates: Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, Schedule gate, 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke. Still `in_progress`: Test Core 1–8, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint (ESLint, repo & tooling gates, docs & code guards, CI/release/engine gates, scoped slot lookup & corpus, scoped query-options erasure). No conclusion was `failure` at this reading; the seat lands only once the in-progress families converge green, as its own rule already says.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `MapConfigSchema`: unchanged — right.** The one hunk in the hits file replaces the `.describe()` string on `outputVariable` (L1490); the key, its `flowBoundVariableNameSchema('outputVariable').optional()` schema and every sibling key are as on `main`. Nothing an author writes is accepted or refused differently.
- **Published spec surface: the JSON-Schema `description` of `MapConfigSchema.outputVariable` changes — right, and complete.** `git grep` of the old sentence on `origin/main` finds exactly two carriers, the Zod source and `content/docs/references/automation/builtin-node-config.mdx`; the head carries the new sentence in both. No other generated artifact holds this describe, so the regeneration is whole (Spec property liveness and Check Changeset are green).
- **Runtime value of `outputVariable` / the map node's `results` widens: an element may be `{ $status: 'cancelled', $itemRunId }` — right under ruling A.** `map-node.ts` pushes the marker into `state.results` on the handoff, `variables.set(outVar, state.results)` binds the same array, and the downstream reader sees it at the item's index (test 1 pins `results[0]` is the marker and `results[1]` item 2's output).
- **`count` = items that ran — right.** `count` is the length of `state.results` with every `isMapItemCancelledMarker` element filtered out; `null` results of items that ran without output still count, markers do not. The step `metrics` (`selected` / `acted` / `failures`) never see the cancelled item: `creditChildRun` credits a paused item only when its child bubbles, and a cancelled child never does.
- **`resume()` gains a continuation and a second refusal arm — right, with one text gap (④ S1).** `refuseGatedResume` now answers `AutomationResult | GatedResumeContinuation | null`; `resume` routes a continuation into `resumeInternal(runId, continueWith, false)`. The arm order is unchanged for every other node (authority first, the still-suspended 409 second, the new gate third and only for `nodeType === 'map'` with a `map:` correlation and no successor in the chain). An item row gone whose history is not `cancelled` — including `getRun` degrading to `null` — is refused `409 RESUME_CHILD_PENDING` with nothing touched; that is the ruling's own "a map that cannot record it refuses" and the triage's "no silent skip either way". The arm narrows one runtime behaviour that used to succeed (the consumed-strand / completed-without-bubble case advanced silently); that silent advance is the defect the card measured, so refusing it is the accepted shape.
- **Public API of `@objectstack/service-automation`: unchanged — right.** `src/index.ts` re-exports a named list from `./engine.js` that does not include `engineBuilt`; `MapItemCancelledMarker`, `isMapItemCancelledMarker`, `mapItemCancelledVariable` and `GatedResumeContinuation` are package-internal module exports. The HTTP door cannot carry the `ENGINE_BUILT_SIGNAL` symbol, so no transport can mint the continuation.
- **The Studio form text (`configSchema.properties.outputVariable.description` in `map-node.ts`) says the same thing — right**, so the online form and the published spec agree.
- **`docs-drift-check` rows:** `flows.mdx` is edited in this PR; `actions-as-tools.mdx` and `approvals.mdx` are listed only through the `getRun` route anchor, and the diff adds `getRun` as a host field on `RunResumeHost`, not a change to the route or the client method — no re-verification owed.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27971-map-cancelled-item.md`: `@objectstack/service-automation: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`; both declaration lines present and identical to the PR body (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`), `Ruling-ref: 6523833308`, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Check Changeset and Lint · PM dispatch-gates (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration`) are green on the head.
- **Clause-②: `yes (widening)` — right.** The published spec's description widens what an `outputVariable` element may be; nothing is taken away from any consumer and no author-writable key is removed or refused, so `(narrowing)` does not apply.
- **Metadata-protocol: `added` — accepted on the ruling's stated reading.** The diff adds no author-writable key or accepted value (`MapConfigSchema` keeps every key; ① above); what it adds is a readable output shape an author's CEL may now branch on (`results[i]['$status']`). The ruling 6523833308 and the director's brief 6523502465 both fixed the arm as `added` with "a readable output shape, no new authored key — the seat confirms the arm from the diff", and the diff confirms exactly that premise: one shape added, none removed, narrowed or re-meant. Under AGENTS.md's wording alone ("what a metadata author can write") a strict reader could call it `none`/`patch`; the ruling settled the arm, and `added` takes at least `minor` on both packages the diff moves — so **`minor` / `minor` matches what the diff publishes**.
- The title's `!` banner is consistent with the runtime change (an element of `results` may now be a marker, and a formerly-succeeding resume may now answer 409); the changeset body states the FROM → TO in prose and the ADR-0087 disposition is the one the gate accepted. Nothing an author writes is renamed, so no tombstone is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag — "the marker's keys are the dev's proposal; the ruling leaves their exact spelling to the contract review."** Fixed here: the marker is `{ $status: 'cancelled', $itemRunId }` exactly as the head spells it — `$status` a closed string literal `'cancelled'`, `$itemRunId` the cancelled item's run id as `getRun` records it; two keys, `$`-led, no third key (`isMapItemCancelledMarker` requires exactly two). The collision claim holds in the cited code: a child flow's `output` is built only from its `isOutput` variables keyed by `v.name` (engine.ts L5999–6005), and `FlowSchema.variables[].name` is `flowBoundVariableNameSchema('variableName')`, a regex that refuses a `$`-led name and is emitted as `pattern` in the published JSON Schema. No real item output can carry a `$status` key.
- **Dev out-of-scope finding (carrier: this review) — the `plugin-approvals` revise-window recall calls `cancelRun` on the run parked at the approval; on a batch sign-off that run is a map item.** Answered: under A the recall now leaves the batch parked on a slot that a later parent-id resume records as `cancelled` and continues past — no longer the skip the card measured, and no longer the stranding C would have caused. What remains is that nothing wakes the parent after the recall: the recall caller never reads `cancelRun`'s boolean and never resumes the parent, so the batch waits for an operator's parent-id resume. That is a producer-side gap, read not measured, outside this PR's surface. **Escalated to the seat to file as its own card** (plugin-approvals: after a revise-window recall of a map item, who resumes the batch, and should the recall say so?). Not a finding against this head.
- `open_questions: []` in the final os-dev-report 6526540343 — none to answer.
- PR body `Skills-docs: none` — confirmed: `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`'s `map` row (L67) describes neither `results`, `count` nor the 409, so no skill text describes the shape that changes.
- Docs half and rider: landed on `main` through PR #28101 (client docblock L5948, README L310, checklist row L1731, `resolveSuspensionChain` seeded with the root id — all present on `origin/main`); this PR is the main fix only. No single-writer breach: the PR-body guards are green.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts` (the one `hits` file) against ruling A and its first consumer — holds.** The describe sentence makes four claims; each is read against the runtime on the same head:

1. *"An item whose run was cancelled keeps its slot as the closed marker `{ $status: 'cancelled', $itemRunId }`."* — `continuePastCancelledMapItem` reads `getRun(itemRunId)`, continues only on `status === 'cancelled'`, and the map pushes the marker on re-entry. The slot is right: at the suspend `state.started = idx + 1` with `results.length === idx`; the marker is pushed before the loop, so `results.length === started` and the loop resumes at item `idx + 1`. The `$mapItemDone` branch cannot fire on the same entry (a cancelled child never bubbles), so no double push. Through a `subflow` link the same signal object is delegated down (`resumeInternal(childRunId, signal, true)`), so the symbol tag survives and the handoff lands in the inner run's scope; the outer leg then rebuilds its own signal (`buildSubflowResumeSignal`), so nothing leaks upward. Test 2 pins it.
2. *"closed"* — `isMapItemCancelledMarker` is exact-two-keys; the Studio description says the same shape. A caller cannot forge it: `applyResumeSignal` rejects any `$`-led or `.$` name unless the signal is engine-built, the gate declines to build a continuation when the caller's own bag already fails that check (a dry `applyResumeSignal` over a fresh map at `link.nodeId` returns a non-empty rejected list), and `resumeInternal` then answers `400 INVALID_SIGNAL` with the run still parked (test 5). Folding a clean caller bag into the engine-built signal is safe because it already passed the `$` check.
3. *"never an output"* — a child output is `{ [v.name]: … }` over `isOutput` variables whose names cannot start with `$` (③ above). Holds.
4. *"not counted as a run"* — `count` filters markers; no step metric credits a cancelled item. Holds.

Break attempts that did not break it: a `null` output from an item that ran is not a marker (counted, as it should be); a run whose correlation is `map:` but whose node type is not the built-in `map` (`map_items` in the concurrent-replica test) is left alone by the `nodeType !== 'map'` guard; a ring-buffer eviction of the cancelled history with no durable store turns the case into the no-record 409 — the ruling's own refusal arm, loud and nothing moved; a corrupt chain cannot reach the gate with a successor because the still-suspended 409 runs first.

**Must-fix: none.**

**Should-fix S1 — the second arm of `RESUME_CHILD_PENDING` is not in the code's own contract text, and its message names no remedy.** The code's definition in `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` (L525–535), the ledger comment in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (L1326), the client docblock `packages/client/src/index.ts` (L5948), the service README (L310) and the checklist row `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/automation.json` (L1731) all say the item "is still suspended; resume the child run the message names". The new arm (row gone, history not `cancelled`) names a run that cannot be resumed, and its `error` text stops at "Nothing was changed" — the operator's only remedy (cancel the parent run) is unstated. The card body itself foresaw this widening ("the code's spec docblock says the item 'is still suspended'"). Only `flows.mdx` describes both arms. One sentence in each of the five places, plus the remedy in the refusal message; the contract docblock in `packages/spec` is governed, so it rides with the seat's landing or a docs-only follow-up under this card. Not a FAIL: the code is an unchanged member of the closed union with its 409 mapping intact, the ruling itself chose this code for the refusal, and no consumer branches on the sentence.

**Should-fix S2 — escalation, not a change to this head:** the plugin-approvals recall gap in ③, filed as its own card by the seat.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-2p9rtc`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czVnUdQQCVKSW5J2uk`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review (delta) · PR #28176 · head 8ec36611 · 2026-10-30T16:35Z

Delta: one commit 8ec36611 on top of the PASSED head 84b980b3 (7 files, +28/-6), read with `git show`/`git diff`; nothing checked out, built or run. Check-runs on 8ec36611 via REST at this reading: 41 `success`, 9 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 in progress.

### S1 disposition

S1 (second `RESUME_CHILD_PENDING` arm absent from the five contract texts; refusal message named no remedy) — **addressed.** All five carriers now state both arms, and the message in `continuePastCancelledMapItem` (run-resume.ts L577–581) ends with the remedy. Still-suspended arm → "resume the named item run"; row-gone-without-`cancelled` arm → "cancel the parent run"; cancelled item → recorded in its slot, map continues. Each matches the runtime: the gate returns the refusal before any state is touched (the continuation is built only on `status === 'cancelled'`), and `refuseMapItemSkip` keeps the first arm unchanged.

### Checks

1. **Five places, both arms.** `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` L534–540 (names the three sub-cases "no entry, an unreadable store, or another status" = the code's `item?.status !== 'cancelled'`; "Nothing moves"; remedy = cancel parent or retry once readable; cancelled item recorded). `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` L1326 row comment (both arms, both remedies; still one `'RESUME_CHILD_PENDING'` literal, position in the owner array unchanged). `packages/client/src/index.ts` L5948–5951 (both arms under the "refusals that leave the suspension intact" lead; does not restate the cancelled-item record — acceptable, it is a refusal list). README L310–313 and checklist variant L1731 (both arms, "nothing moves", cancelled item recorded). `flows.mdx` unchanged and already consistent. Terminology "parent run" = the map's own run throughout, the same run the message names.
2. **Remedy is true.** `cancelRun(link.runId)` (run-resume.ts L823–) does `loadSuspendedRunStrict` → `forgetSuspendedRun(run, 'cancelled')` → `recordLog(status: 'cancelled')`; the map's run is the suspension parked on `map:<item>`, so cancelling it is exactly what ends the batch. Cancellation never cascades (engine docblock: "never touches the parent"), so in the nested case the caller's run `runId` stays parked on its `subflow:` link and must be cancelled too — "and run 'OUTER', which waits on it" is right, and `runId` = chain[0] is the caller's run. "Retry once readable": `getRun` (run-history.ts L317–) degrades a thrown `store.loadTerminal` to `null` under a `warn`, and the in-memory journal is consulted first, so a later read of the same id after store recovery answers `cancelled` and the resume then mints the continuation; conditional wording ("if the store was unreachable") keeps it true for the no-row case, which is not transient. Gap: for a chain deeper than two (OUTER → MID → MAP, `MAX_SUSPENSION_CHAIN_DEPTH` 32 allows it) the message names only `link.runId` and `runId`; intermediate runs stay parked unnamed — see Should-fix.
3. **No contract change beyond text.** Code literal, owner array, `ErrorCode` union and the 409 mapping untouched (delta touches only the row's `//` comment). No generator consumes that comment: `check-generated.ts`'s only ledger entry is `check:error-code-provenance` ("no artifact"), `export-origins/api.json` maps symbols not comments, and `git grep` of the old sentence on the head finds only the three edited source carriers (plus an unrelated line in `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`). Spec CI families (Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Lint) green. Changeset: the existing `.changeset/27971-map-cancelled-item.md` already states the second arm ("Nothing to record is refused … 409 RESUME_CHILD_PENDING before anything moves") and bumps `@objectstack/spec` minor; a message-wording change on an existing refusal needs no further line.
4. **Pin bites.** `map-cancelled-item-resume.test.ts` L183 and L200 assert `toContain("To end the batch, cancel run '${paused.runId}'")` where `paused.runId` is the batch_flow (map) run, distinct from `item1.runId`; removing or re-targeting the remedy fails both. The nested wording ("and run '…', which waits on it") has no pin.
5. **Checklist JSON** parses; item `revision` 9 → 10 and the new history row `{ revision: 10, date, change, ref: "#27971" }` matches its neighbours (rows 7–9) and `check-platform-checklist.mjs` L3395's rule that `revision` equals the last history entry's revision. `variants` line edited in place; no acceptance clause changed.

### Must-fix
